I build and audit evaluations for **tool-using agents**, with a focus on measurement validity: whether
an eval's number means what it is taken to mean.

Most of my work starts from a specific worry. An agentic eval makes claims about what the model knew,
what it did, and what the scorer saw — and each of those can fail on its own, quietly, while the run
reports success. The three projects below are one line of work on those three failures, in that order.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Code & experiments → [github.com/raina-sid/inspect-eval-replications](https://github.com/raina-sid/inspect-eval-replications)**

Environments, scorers and per-cell results for the work below, plus the audit scripts that re-derive
every published figure from raw logs without trusting my own scorers.
:::

## An eval makes three claims. Each can fail quietly.

### 1. Harness validity — can the environment control what the model knows?

**[What's the right way to filter tool outputs in Inspect?](posts/filtering-tool-outputs-in-inspect.qmd)**
· Aug 2026

The interception point that looks correct **fails open silently.** If a filter raises, Inspect's
`_emit_to_all` swallows the exception: the model receives unfiltered input and the eval still passes,
with the control skipped and nothing in the log to say so.

*Demonstrates:* reading a framework's internals to establish where a control can actually be enforced,
and the difference between a control that is missing and one that is present but unenforceable. Filed
as [an open question to the maintainers](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai/issues/5020)
rather than a complaint, with a runnable repro that needs no API key.

### 2. Benchmark validity — does the task still elicit the behaviour?

**[69% → 11% → 0%: three generations on Apollo's insider-trading eval](posts/insider-trading-eval-saturated.qmd)**
· Sep 2026

The 2023 result **replicates** on its target model — 63.3% [45.5, 78.1] against the authors' own labels
— and **bounds below 1%** on `gpt-5.5` (0/300, one-sided exact upper bound 0.99%). But **298 of those
300 runs leave the authored scenario on turn one.** The zero measures departure from the script, not
resolution of the dilemma.

*Demonstrates:* faithful replication as the first step rather than the last, calibration against the
original authors' labels, and recognising when a benchmark has saturated so that its headline number
has stopped carrying information.
[Code](https://github.com/raina-sid/inspect-eval-replications/tree/main/src/evalrep/insider_trading)

### 3. Metric validity — does the scorer detect the behaviour?

**[When do AI agents leak restricted information?](posts/when-agents-leak-restricted-information.qmd)**
· Sep 2026

A data policy naming the restricted *field* leaked it **30/30**. Naming the **tool-call channel** took
it to **0/503**. Then, under pressure, the same policy held the string while information derived from
it kept reaching the outbound channel — with the exact-match metric reading zero.

*Demonstrates:* a policy ladder with an emphasis control that rules out the obvious confound; three
proposed mechanisms retracted when later cells refuted them; and an audit that re-derives every figure
from raw logs, which caught two of my own published numbers, one of them sign-inverted.
[Code](https://github.com/raina-sid/inspect-eval-replications/tree/main/src/evalrep/secret_propagation)

## Research interests

- **Agent evaluations** — tool-using agents in environments where the information available to the
  agent is the experimental condition
- **Evaluation validity** — harness, benchmark and metric failures, and how to tell them apart from
  results
- **Information-flow and tool-use safety** — what an agent can be prevented from emitting, and by
  which mechanism
- **Benchmark design and auditing** — replication, saturation, and re-deriving reported figures from
  primary logs

## Who's writing this

A data scientist, twelve years in industry, based in Berlin. Most of that was forecasting and
recommender systems in production — demand models and ranking, where the metric is easy to compute and
what it licenses you to say is not. That turned out to be better preparation for eval work than I
expected: it is the same question either way, which is whether the number you can compute is the number
you actually wanted.

A merged contribution to [`inspect_ai`](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai)
([PR #4913](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai/pull/4913)), the eval framework maintained
by the UK AI Security Institute · [All writing](writing.qmd) ·
